newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian Opposition targets budget measures.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian Opposition targets budget measures.

text.p: Australia's Labor opposition said on Tuesday it would oppose some of the Liberal-National government's budget measures now in parliament.
A party spokesman, speaking to reporters, said these measures would be opposed:
-- The introduction of a two year waiting period for student income support for newly arrived migrants, which would save A$6 million in 1996/97, rising to A$13 million in 1999/00;
-- The cut in the tax deductibility of research and development spending to 125 percent from 150 percent, which would increase revenue by A$35 million in 1996/97, rising to A$440 million in 1999/00;
-- The removal of the tax deductibility that co-operatives get on borrowings from government lending bodies, which would increase revenue by A$2 million in 1997/98, rising to A$6 million in 1999/00.
The spokesman also said Labor might oppose the abolition of a syndication system for research and development.
It would back the abolition if the government could show that the system was being abused and, in any case, it would not oppose tightening up of some of the syndication rules.
Government sources say that pressure from the ruling coalition's National Party has led to the plan for co-operative's loans being scaled back.
It was to begin on budget night, August 20, but will now not affect any loans taken before 1998.
The change has not been announced.
The government's budget cuts will save A$3.9 billion in the current fiscal year to June, rising to A$7.2 billion in 1997/98.
Budget measures that require legislation are subject to the consent of parliament's upper house of parliament, the Senate, where the government does not have a majority.
It needs the support from at least two non-government senators in the 76-seat chamber.
